ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary legislation is Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, including Law 11/2021 of 9 July. Implementing rules are Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May. The Central Register of Beneficial Ownership is governed principally by Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July. Corporate beneficial-ownership information is also collected through notarial and Mercantile Registry systems. Obliged entities must apply customer due diligence, identify and verify beneficial owners, maintain records, report suspicious activity to SEPBLAC, and comply with record-retention and internal-control requirements.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and onboarding, screen the company, directors, authorized representatives, UBOs, controlling persons, and material counterparties against United Nations sanctions, European Union sanctions, Spanish sanctions and restrictive-measures information, and applicable domestic law-enforcement or terrorism-financing lists. Screen against OFAC lists as a mandatory internal control where there is a United States person, US-dollar clearing, US financial institution, US technology, or other US nexus; OFAC is not generally a standalone Spanish-law obligation without such nexus. Conduct PEP and close-associate screening under Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014, obtain senior-management approval for PEP relationships, establish source of wealth and source of funds, apply enhanced monitoring, document false-positive resolution, and rescreen periodically and upon trigger events.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central online services at https://www.rmc.es; incorporation may also be coordinated through the CIRCE/PAE system at https://paeelectronico.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be unique and comply with the Spanish Companies Registry Regulations and the Spanish Capital Companies Act. The name must include the legal-form designation or abbreviation, such as Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada or S.L. Names may use Spanish or other legally acceptable languages and Latin characters, but must not create confusion with an existing registered name, imply an unauthorized public or regulated status, or use misleading expressions. Foreign-language names may require a clear transliteration or explanatory treatment where necessary for registry identification. The name certificate does not itself authorize a regulated activity or protect a trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Existing or confusingly similar registered corporate names

Terms suggesting a public authority, government body, municipality, royal institution, or official status, including España, Nacional, Estatal, Real, Oficial, and similar expressions, unless legally justified and accepted

Regulated financial, insurance, securities, banking, credit, investment, or payment terms, including Banco, Bank, Seguro, Insurance, Valores, Bolsa, Crédito, Financiera, and similar expressions, unless the relevant authorization or justification exists
Terms suggesting a licensed professional or regulated activity where the company lacks the required authorization or qualified professional structure
Expressions contrary to law, public order, morality, or likely to mislead the public
Protected names, emblems, and designations of international organizations, public institutions, or protected public-interest bodies
Terms conflicting with registered trademarks or trade names, subject to separate Spanish Patent and Trademark Office analysis
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Request a negative certification of corporate name from the Registro Mercantil Central. The certification generally supports incorporation for three months from issuance, while the name reservation is generally maintained for six months; the deed must therefore be executed and submitted within the applicable statutory periods. If rejected, obtain the written rejection reason, verify similarity, prohibited terminology, legal-form wording, and documentary defects, and submit a correction or replacement application through the Registro Mercantil Central. A formal administrative challenge may be filed with the competent registry authority within the applicable procedural deadline stated in the notice, ordinarily using the administrative remedies available under Law 39/2015 on the Common Administrative Procedure. A registry decision affecting registration may also be challenged through the Mercantile Registry appeal process before the Directorate-General competent for legal security and public faith, followed by judicial review where available. A new name application is normally faster than litigation where the rejection is based on similarity or sensitive wording.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must have a registered office in Spain capable of receiving official notices and supporting the company's actual administrative or management location. A virtual office may be acceptable for a CAD/BIM outsourcing business if it is a genuine serviced address, the provider lawfully permits registration, mail and official notices are promptly handled, and the company maintains adequate records and operational evidence. A mailbox-only arrangement, false address, or address disconnected from management and business activity creates tax, registry, AML, banking, and substance risks. The activity described does not ordinarily require a special establishment license, but engineering services involving reserved professional acts, signing or certifying construction projects, or statutory responsibility may require qualified professionals, professional-body compliance, and additional authorization. The company should separately verify Spanish tax registration, IAE activity classification, data-protection compliance, labor status, and any applicable professional-qualification requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Indicative risk: approximately 5-15 percent annually for a low-risk, properly registered CAD/BIM company with coherent tax, banking, AML, and address records; approximately 20-40 percent during the first two years if the company uses a high-volume virtual-office provider, has nonresident management, inconsistent business evidence, unusual cross-border payments, delayed tax filings, or AML alerts. These percentages are risk estimates, not statutory probabilities. Spanish tax authorities, municipal authorities, banks, SEPBLAC-obliged entities, and labor authorities may conduct document requests or on-site checks without advance notice where legally permitted.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Spanish State Tax Administration Agency; e-Portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Operational units: Departamento de Gestión Tributaria (registration and census), Departamento de Inspección Financiera y Tributaria (audits), and Oficina Nacional de Gestión de Grandes Empresas for large taxpayers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the SL before a Spanish notary (deed of incorporation), register the company in the Mercantile Registry, and obtain the provisional corporate NIF issued by the notary at the incorporation event. Step 2 — File Form 036 (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) with the AEAT attaching the notarized deed, Mercantile Registry certificate, power of attorney granted to a Spanish-domiciled fiscal representative, and identification documents of all non-resident shareholders, in order to receive the definitive corporate NIF (9 characters: letter B for SL plus 8 digits). Step 3 — Each non-resident shareholder or foreign entity obtains its own NIF-NIE (Form 030 and Form 036, through the AEAT, a Spanish Consulate, or the appointed representative); a fiscal representative domiciled in Spain must be designated for the SL under art. 10 of the Ley General Tributaria. Step 4 — The definitive NIF is issued immediately or within 1–3 business days; the company must then complete its registration by filing Form 036 to declare commencement of activities under IVA and Impuesto sobre Sociedades. Step 5 — For CAD/BIM export operations, register in the SGA/EX system for customs declarations, and elect to join REDEME (monthly VAT return register) where cash-flow refunds are desired.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation and Territorial_Scope = Worldwide_Net_Income for the SL as a Spanish resident corporate taxpayer under Ley 27/2014 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades). Headline corporate rate: 25%; newly created SLs may enjoy 15% for the first two profitable tax periods (art. 29.1 LIS). The SL is not a pass-through entity: non-resident shareholders are subject to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) at 19% withholding on dividend distributions, subject to treaty relief. CAD/BIM service revenue is included in the Spanish taxable base, with foreign tax credit available under art. 31–32 LIS. Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable to a mainland Spanish SL; the Canary Islands ZEC regime is limited to island-based entities and cannot be elected by the reference entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no check-the-box regime for corporations. Available elections and special regimes: (i) consolidated tax group filing under art. 64–75 LIS where the parent holds 75% of a Spanish subsidiary for an uninterrupted pre-tax period; (ii) reduced 15% new-enterprise rate under art. 29.1 LIS; (iii) OSS/IOSS special VAT schemes for intra-EU distance sales of goods and electronic services (art. 61–66 LIVA), not relevant to B2B engineering services; (iv) monthly VAT return election by joining REDEME; (v) EBITDA-based interest limitation election vs group ratio rule under art. 16.4 LIS; (vi) hybrid mismatch treatment under EU ATAD (art. 15–15 ter LIS) is compulsory with no elective exclusion; the SL must evidence absence of hybrid deduction/non-inclusion mismatches in its intercompany documentation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Value Added Tax) governed by Ley 37/1992 and Real Decreto 1624/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum turnover threshold for Spanish-established businesses: any entity habitually engaging in economic activity, including remote CAD/BIM services to foreign clients, must file Form 036/037 and obtain a Spanish VAT number before the first transaction (art. 164.1 LIVA). For non-established foreign suppliers, B2B services to Spanish businesses are subject to the reverse-charge mechanism and do not trigger mandatory local registration; for B2C digitally supplied services, the intra-EU threshold of EUR 10,000 per calendar year applies, after which registration in OSS becomes mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal clearance applies through the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) for large enterprises (turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04), VAT groups, and REDEME members: each invoice record must be transmitted to the AEAT via authenticated web-service API within 4 business days of issuance (8-day transitional accommodation permitted at initial implementation). The Verifactu standard (Real Decreto 1007/2023, in force since 21 December 2023) requires all invoicing software to be certified, generating a cryptographically chained record ledger (HashEncadenado), a unique QR signature, and full traceability of invoice events; there is no physical fiscal stamp in Spain, but the Verifactu hash chain functions as the digital seal. Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) mandates structured electronic invoicing (Facturae / PEPPOL-UBL) for all B2B transactions within the implementation waves scheduled for 2025–2026; penalties for failure to emit or receive compliant e-invoices are set in art. 201 bis LGT at EUR 1,000–10,000 per infringement, rising to EUR 10,000–40,000 where the conduct obstructs AEAT verification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: CAD/BIM and civil-engineering services supplied by the Spanish SL to a foreign business are outside the scope of Spanish VAT (no sujeto a IVA) under the B2B place-of-supply rule of art. 70.1.1º LIVA, provided the recipient is a taxable person established outside Spain and the service is not abused or effectively used in the Spanish customs territory. The invoice must be issued at 0% VAT with the legal caption referencing art. 70.1.1º LIVA and, where the client is an EU taxable person, indicate that the transaction is subject to reverse charge in the client's member state. For physical goods bundled with offshore civil-works projects, the Spanish 0% export exemption (art. 21 LIVA) applies only if the goods physically leave EU customs territory within 90 days of the customs declaration, as evidenced by a valid MRN exit record and transport documentation. Substantiation criteria: (a) validation of the client's EU VAT ID in VIES or a foreign tax residence certificate; (b) the client's establishment outside Spanish territory; (c) direct connection of the services to the client's business activity; and (d) a complete export compliance file maintained contemporaneously.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA) generated in the SGA/EX system with valid MRN and exit certification for any physical goods
Bill of Lading (B/L), CMR, or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing physical departure from EU customs territory within 90 days
Inward Remittance Certificate — bank SWIFT credit statement evidencing settlement of the export consideration from the non-resident client's account
Signed CAD/BIM or Engineering Services Agreement including scope, deliverables, milestones, contract value, and place of use
Commercial Invoice itemized in the contract currency, issued without Spanish VAT, referencing the applicable legal basis (art. 70.1.1º LIVA or art. 21 LIVA)
VIES validation output or foreign tax certificate establishing the customer's non-resident taxable status
Delivery confirmation (client acceptance certificate or transmittal sheet) evidencing completion of the offshore service
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may reopen the 0% or no-subjection position within the 4-year limitation period (art. 66 LGT) and claw back the full amount of VAT refunded plus late-payment interest (art. 26 LGT). Sanctions apply under art. 191 LGT (50%–150% of the misdeclared VAT), art. 195 LGT (50% proportional penalty for improperly obtained refunds), and art. 201 bis LGT for e-invoicing software defects. Where the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000, the matter constitutes a criminal offence (delito contra la Hacienda Pública, art. 305 Código Penal) carrying imprisonment of 1 to 5 years, extension of the limitation period to 10 years, and loss of public subsidies and procurement capacity. Failure to repatriate the invoiced consideration into Spain within the 180-day window gives rise to a rebuttable presumption of fictitious export, leading to full reassessment, interest, and penalty aggravation to the upper sanction bracket; a robust contemporaneous export file (export ledger, credit evidence, client acceptance records, annual confirmation letters) mitigates toward the minimum 50% penalty tier.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under a fully convertible Eurozone currency regime. Capital account transactions, including equity injections, profit remittances, and intercompany loans, are unrestricted for EU-resident entities with no prior approval required. Non-resident shareholders face standard Spanish withholding tax (19% on dividends) and EU reporting obligations under DAC6 and CRS; no capital controls apply to legitimate cross-border flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or repatriation of export proceeds is required under Spanish law. Exporters must register with AEAT for VAT purposes and provide commercial invoices, shipping documents, and proof of payment to banks for FX transactions. All cross-border receipts trigger mandatory AML/CFT reporting above €10,000 threshold.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Wise and similar EMI platforms are fully viable for low-to-medium volume cross-border transfers with standard AML screening. Full EMI licensing is restricted; high-volume operations require integration with licensed Spanish banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and video identification are permitted for Spanish SL entities under CNMV and Banco de España guidelines. Physical appearance of directors is required only for accounts exceeding €200,000 or when beneficial ownership verification is flagged.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds from high-risk jurisdictions or inconsistent beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized beneficial ownership certificate, tax residency proofs, bank reference letters, and source-of-wealth affidavits

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions linked to crypto or unregulated entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Blockchain analytics reports, third-party audit statements, and FATF-compliant transaction history

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification requires NIF tax ID, Registro Mercantil entry, and beneficial ownership declaration. Local Spanish bank accounts preferred for initial deposits to minimize FX conversion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 for standard payments; Commercial Letters of Credit for trade settlements. All outflows require supporting contracts, invoices, and AML documentation. Purpose codes must align with ISIC 7110 engineering services.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and management report deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepare within three months after financial year-end; approve within six months; deposit within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, filing is normally due by 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure after one year from the filing deadline; directors may incur fines generally ranging from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher limits for larger companies. Closure is not an automatic administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end, normally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without prior notice generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay, or 15% after more than 12 months; prior notice may trigger penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation accompanying the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Mercantile Registry and the Central Registry of Beneficial Ownership where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submit the beneficial ownership declaration with the annual accounts deposit and update it when ownership or control information changes. Changes should be reported promptly, generally within ten days of the relevant change becoming known.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry filing defects, registry closure, and potential anti-money-laundering administrative sanctions; failure to identify or update beneficial ownership may also restrict access to registry services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual third-party transaction information return, Modelo 347, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed during February for reportable transactions in the preceding calendar year, subject to the applicable electronic filing timetable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete, or inaccurate information returns may attract fixed or proportional tax penalties, with amounts depending on the number and significance of omitted or incorrect data.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding and payments-on-account information returns, including Modelos 180 and 190, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed in January for the preceding calendar year; exact dates follow the Tax Agency electronic filing calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate filing may generate fixed information-return penalties and, where withholding was unpaid, surcharges, interest, and penalties based on the unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return, Modelo 390, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed during the first 30 calendar days of January for the preceding year, unless the company falls within an applicable exemption or uses the immediate supply information regime.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete, or inaccurate filing may result in fixed penalties; unpaid VAT additionally attracts interest, surcharges, and tax penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when, for two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: EUR 2.85 million in total assets, EUR 5.7 million in net annual turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional mandatory audit rules apply to public-interest entities, certain regulated entities, entities receiving qualifying subsidies, and companies required to prepare consolidated accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish accounting legislation. IFRS is mandatory for listed consolidated groups and may apply to other qualifying consolidated reporting situations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify its ultimate beneficial owners and confirm the information with the annual accounts deposit. Any change in direct or indirect ownership or control must be reflected through the applicable Mercantile Registry and beneficial ownership filing procedures without undue delay, generally within ten days of becoming aware of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' and management-body resolutions
Register of Sole-Shareholder Contracts, if the company is or becomes a sole-member company
Accounting books and annual financial statements
Current director and beneficial ownership information maintained for registry and anti-money-laundering purposes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 325-1,300 per year, depending on address, mail handling, corporate secretarial support, and electronic notification services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-8,000 for a small Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requiring a statutory audit; no statutory audit fee applies if the company remains below the mandatory audit thresholds
